heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S prints Bambu PLA-CF exceptionally well up to a calculated safe speed of 190 mm/s capped by its 16 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. However, you must upgrade the stock stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears to hardened steel to prevent rapid abrasive wear.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate (clean with warm water and dish soap; no adhesive needed)
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 16 mm³/s in the filament settings to eliminate underextrusion during high-speed moves.
Adjust Pressure Advance to approximately 0.024 and run dynamic flow calibration via OrcaSlicer for carbon-fiber filled resin.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 1 mm and set Retraction Distance to 0.8 mm to reduce stringing and nozzle buildup.
Vent the chamber by propping open the top glass lid or front door during long prints to prevent PLA heat creep and cold-end clogging.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking and severe underextrusion midway through a print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Heat creep caused by printing low-softening-temp PLA in a closed enclosure, or partial nozzle clogging from carbon fiber clusters in a 0.4mm orifice.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Crack the top glass lid or front door to drop chamber temp below 35°C, perform a cold pull, and maintain nozzle temperature at 225°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Premature nozzle wear causing blown-out line widths and poor dimensional accuracy
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: The abrasive carbon fibers within Bambu PLA-CF quickly erode the factory P1S stainless steel nozzle orifice.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Replace the stock hotend and extruder gear assembly with genuine Bambu Lab hardened steel components.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough, brittle perimeters and excessive surface fuzz/hair stringing
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption by the PLA matrix and carbon fiber content boiling off inside the meltzone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool in a filament dryer at 55°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing, and store with active desiccant in the AMS.

faq.question: Can I print Bambu PLA-CF using the stock P1S 0.4mm stainless steel hotend?
faq.answer: Technically yes, but only for a very short duration. The carbon fibers will quickly erode the stock stainless steel nozzle and gears within 1 to 2 spools, causing poor extrusion quality and ruined tolerances. Upgrading to hardened steel is strongly recommended.

faq.question: Should I keep the P1S door closed or open when printing PLA-CF?
faq.answer: Keep the door cracked open or the top glass lid propped. Even with carbon fiber filling, the base polymer is standard PLA with a low glass transition temperature (~55°C), making it prone to heat creep clogging in a fully enclosed chamber.

faq.question: Is Bambu PLA-CF fully compatible with the standard AMS unit?
faq.answer: Yes, Bambu PLA-CF is formulated and tested to feed safely through the AMS without brittle snapping, provided it is properly dried and you use hardened extruder components downstream.

faq.question: Does PLA-CF require a 0.6mm nozzle, or is 0.4mm sufficient?
faq.answer: A 0.4mm hardened nozzle works reliably with Bambu PLA-CF because the chopped carbon fibers are milled short enough to avoid clogs under normal conditions, though a 0.6mm nozzle provides an extra safety margin against clogging.
